title: Package-provided flows are read-only in Studio — no design mode and no node inspector on any node, which makes every checklist clause needing a node panel on a *shipped* flow unreachable (fixture limit for QA, but a product question worth a ruling)
body:
Restart-when: any objectui PR touches the Studio flow-designer node inspector (ride along with a read-only inspection view for package-provided flows), or a customer reports needing to debug a shipped flow in production

## Symptom

Opening a **package-provided (shipped) flow** in Studio offers **no design mode and no node inspector for any node**. There is no panel from which a node's configuration can be read, so any verification step that needs to look at a shipped flow's node config cannot be performed at all.

Concrete cost in the automation run — two clauses went `blocked(fixture)` rather than pass or fail:

- `time-relative-trigger` — clause 0;
- `connector-dispatch-matrix` — clause 3.

**Verified contrast:** a **writable draft** flow *does* open the inspector. So this is not a broken inspector; it is that the inspector is unavailable specifically on flows that arrived via a package.

## Two readings, both recorded honestly

The run classified this as a **fixture limit, not a product defect**, and that classification is reasonable: packages install read-only, the writable-draft path works, and the checklist's clauses could be satisfied against a draft fixture instead.

But the other reading deserves a maintainer's glance rather than being buried in a run's fixture list: **"you cannot inspect a shipped flow's nodes in Studio" is a plausible product gap.** Inspection is a *read*. Read-only correctly forbids editing a package's flow; it does not obviously imply the operator may not see how a shipped flow's nodes are configured — and an operator debugging a package flow in production has exactly that need. Whether design mode is the right vehicle for a read-only inspection view is the question; that is a product call, not a QA call.

This card asks for that ruling, and records the QA-side consequence either way. If the ruling is "working as intended", the follow-up is fixture-side (give the affected checklist clauses a writable draft flow to drive, or mark the clauses shipped-flow-inapplicable). If the ruling is "operators should be able to inspect a shipped flow", the fix is cross-repo in objectui's Studio.

## Root cause

**Not located by the run** beyond the observed boundary: package-provided flows open without design mode, while a writable draft opens the inspector normally. No Studio source was traced to the gate that decides this.

## Reproduction

1. Boot showcase (the shipped showcase package provides several flows) and open Studio.
2. Open any package-provided flow — e.g. one of the showcase flows exercised by `time-relative-trigger` / `connector-dispatch-matrix`.
3. Observe: no design mode; clicking any node opens no inspector panel.
4. Control: create a writable draft flow and open it — clicking a node opens the inspector as expected.

## Lane

No `domain:*` label applied deliberately: the landing place depends on the ruling above and is genuinely ambiguous between three candidates — the QA checklist under `docs/qa/platform-checklist/` (devx), the showcase fixtures under `examples/app-showcase/` (automation subsystem), and objectui's Studio (cross-repo). Labelling it now would guess at the answer this card is asking for.

## Source

Extracted from the QA run objectstack-ai/objectstack#7516 (framework a86db175).
